### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/spec`, touching **7** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **4** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/src/data/datasource-credential-redaction.ts`, `packages/spec/src/data/driver/common.zod.ts`, `packages/spec/src/integration/connector-credential-redaction.ts`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**2** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/automation/connectors.mdx`  _(via /api/v1/automation/connectors (route, a path literal in acceptanceCriteria), /meta/connector/:name (route, a path literal in surface))_
- `content/docs/kernel/cluster.mdx`  _(via /api/v1/automation/connectors (route, a path literal in acceptanceCriteria), /meta/connector/:name (route, a path literal in surface))_

⛔ **3** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v15.mdx`  _(via /api/v1/automation/connectors (route, a path literal in acceptanceCriteria))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-6.mdx`  _(via /meta/connector/:name (route, a path literal in surface))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-3.mdx`  _(via /api/v1/automation/connectors (route, a path literal in acceptanceCriteria))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **4** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/src/data/datasource-credential-redaction.ts`, `packages/spec/src/data/driver/common.zod.ts`, `packages/spec/src/integration/connector-credential-redaction.ts`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **61** of **219** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **158** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **158**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **103** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **170** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a9fb14bdeeb5e09fec341ead4e0fffd8d8ed00bb` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `7f8b1461102fcec535fa99e9fc021c1c468a7a39` — the merge of head `87265453372a5c60d49f0031b7f004afac7cc3cc` into base `a9fb14bdeeb5e09fec341ead4e0fffd8d8ed00bb`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 7f8b1461102fcec535fa99e9fc021c1c468a7a39 && git checkout 7f8b1461102fcec535fa99e9fc021c1c468a7a39
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin a9fb14bdeeb5e09fec341ead4e0fffd8d8ed00bb 87265453372a5c60d49f0031b7f004afac7cc3cc && git checkout -B drift-repro a9fb14bdeeb5e09fec341ead4e0fffd8d8ed00bb && git merge --no-ff 87265453372a5c60d49f0031b7f004afac7cc3cc

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a9fb14bdeeb5e09fec341ead4e0fffd8d8ed00bb
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs a9fb14bdeeb5e09fec341ead4e0fffd8d8ed00bb` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `87265453372a5c60d49f0031b7f004afac7cc3cc`
Local-runs: probe — one `node` run comparing `new URL()` against the head's `urlUserinfoSpan` over 55 strings (mixed-case special schemes, runs of one to five `/`, backslash-only and mixed runs, tab/LF/CR and surrounding spaces, `file:`, non-special schemes, scheme-less `//`, `/\` and `\\`, plain text beginning `http:`); nothing built, no suite or gate re-run
Scope: packages/spec/src/data/datasource-credential-redaction.ts, packages/spec/src/data/driver/common.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/data/driver/url-boundary.ts, packages/spec/src/integration/connector-credential-redaction.ts, packages/spec/src/integration/connector-url-credentials.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.url-credential-special-scheme-read-however-many-slashes.ts, .changeset/url-credential-special-scheme-read-however-many-slashes.md, packages/spec/src/data/datasource-credential-redaction.test.ts, packages/spec/src/data/driver/driver-credential-refusal.test.ts, packages/spec/src/integration/connector-entry-url-credentials.test.ts + packages/services/service-datasource/src/datasource-config-redaction.ts, packages/services/service-datasource/src/datasource-credential-migration.ts, packages/services/service-datasource/src/datasource-admin-service.ts, packages/services/service-datasource/src/default-datasource-driver-factory.ts, packages/spec/src/data/datasource.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/kernel/metadata-type-redaction.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.url-credential-judged-trimmed-and-in-any-connector-string.ts, packages/spec/scripts/build-migration-registry.ts, packages/cli/src/utils/connection-display.ts

Inputs: the PR body and file list, the net diff against `main` at this head (10 files, +359/−20, branched from `1f13eb3189`), the 65 check-runs on the head, PR #29875 (merged) as the precedent in the same family, and the published `@libsql/core@0.18.0` tarball (`lib-esm/uri.js`, `lib-esm/config.js`) for the turso claim. Ruling of record: maintainer 2026-11-04, option A, under ruling D (#29875).

### ① Derived judgments

**One grammar, one function, no `new URL()` at either door.** The only grammar change is `authorityStart()` in `url-boundary.ts`: for a scheme in `{ftp, http, https, ws, wss}` (matched case-insensitively, `SCHEME_RE` is `/i` and the set lookup lowercases) the authority starts after the whole run of `/` and `\` that follows `scheme:`, a run of zero included; every other string falls through to the unchanged `AUTHORITY_START_RE` (`scheme://` or scheme-relative `//`). `urlUserinfoSpan` is the single reader; `authorityStart`, `SCHEME_RE` and `AUTHORITY_SPECIAL_SCHEMES` are module-private and `url-boundary.ts` is not re-exported, so the public surface is unmoved (`check:api-surface` unchanged on the head).

**Per door, refusal ⇔ rewrite holds, by construction and by pin.**
- Connector write door: `DeclarativeConnectorEntrySchema` → `connectorUrlCredentialPartsOf` → `connectorUrlWithoutUserinfo` → `urlUserinfoSpan`. Connector read rewrite: `connector-credential-redaction.ts` → the same `connectorUrlWithoutUserinfo`. One function on both sides; the new block in `connector-entry-url-credentials.test.ts` pins refused ⇔ rewritten over 35 special leads plus 15 no-authority controls, each at three values and two positions (`providerConfig.baseUrl` and a non-URL `providerConfig` string), with the served form re-parsed green.
- Datasource write door: `credentialFreeUrl` on postgres/mysql/mongo/turso `config.url` and turso `config.syncUrl` → `urlUserinfoPassword` → `urlUserinfoSpan`. Datasource read rewrite: `redactDatasourceConfig` → `redactUrlCredentials` → `redactUrlPassword` → `urlUserinfoSpan`, which removes the password and keeps the username, so the served form passes the write door. Pinned per key, `syncUrl` included, in `datasource-credential-redaction.test.ts` (refused ⇔ rewritten over the special and no-authority leads) and `driver-credential-refusal.test.ts` (refusal pathed at the key, bare-username and path-`@` controls, `//` forms keep their reading).
- Unchanged, read and confirmed by the probe: `file:` (not in the set; `file:` with no `//` has no authority, `file:///` an empty one; `file://u:p@h` reads as it did on `main`), every non-special scheme (`postgres:`, `postgresql:`, `mysql:`, `mongodb:`, `libsql:`, `mailto:`, `https+x:`), the scheme-relative `//` form, and every `scheme://` spelling (the special branch skips exactly two characters there, the same offset `AUTHORITY_START_RE` gave). The narrowing is exactly: a special scheme followed by zero, one, or three-or-more slashes/backslashes, or any run holding a `\`, now reads its authority.

**Authority end unchanged**: `rest.search(/[/?#]/)` is untouched; `\` still does not end it. The libsql claim is verified against the published `@libsql/core@0.18.0`: its URI regex takes the authority as an optional `//` followed by a run of characters that are none of `/`, `?` and `#`, and its authority regex takes the userinfo as a username of non-colon characters, an optional colon and a greedy password, then an `@` — so the libsql client ends the authority at `/`, `?`, `#` only and its userinfo at the last `@` — the longer authority the head keeps holds every userinfo either parser reads, and a `\`-ended reading would hold fewer. Two further libsql facts bear on the turso keys: it requires the `//` (`encodeBaseUrl` refuses a URL with no authority) and lowercases the scheme before routing, so no turso datasource spelled a special scheme without exactly `//` ever connected; the narrowing takes away no working turso value.

**service-datasource restore and migration detectors.** `getDatasource()` serves through `redactDatasourceConfig`, so a stored row holding such a value under a URL key is now served with its password removed and the key named in `redactedConfigKeys`; `restoreRedactedConfig` is derived from the same redactor (it grafts the stored leaf back wherever the patch equals the served projection), so a save of the served form keeps the stored value and nothing is silently deleted; the generic metadata door's `metadata-type-redaction.ts` and `redactedPathsCarriedForward` are the same derivation. `planCredentialMigration` → `urlCredentialKeys` (`redactUrlCredentials(value) !== value`) now refuses such a row with the per-row remedy instead of planning `nothing-to-migrate`. This is right: ruling D makes the read rewrite exactly what the write refuses and never re-judges a stored row, and the restore is what keeps the second half true. The two connect-path consumers of the username half (`buildMongoAuth` → `urlUserinfoUsername`, and the mongo "names no user" refinement in `datasource.zod.ts`) read `mongodb:` only, which is not special — unchanged.

**Disclosure (security-findings.md §6).** The title, body, changeset, D3 entry, the three commit messages and every test name state the rule ("read for credentials the way a URL parser reads it, however many slashes follow the scheme"); a grep of all of them and the full diff for mechanism vocabulary returns nothing. The changeset's FROM → TO is the migration mapping a breaking changeset must carry (same form as #29875's). Placeholders are fake; `hunter2` is the pre-existing placeholder of both driver test files on `main`.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/spec` **minor**, title `feat(spec)!:`, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` on both the PR body and the changeset — correct: a `narrowed` kind takes at least minor on the moved package and a narrowing is BREAKING. No other package publishes a change.

D3 entry `packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.url-credential-special-scheme-read-however-many-slashes.ts`: `id` equals the filename stem; the directory is the registry (`loadEntries` reads it with `readdirSync`, there is no index), and the changeset carries the marker `adr-0087: registered url-credential-special-scheme-read-however-many-slashes`; `Lint & Repo Gates` (carries `check:adr-0087-registration`) and `TypeScript Type Check` (carries `check:spec-changes` / `check:upgrade-guide`) are `success` on the head, so it is registered and projects. Its `surface`, `replacement` and `acceptanceCriteria` are the family's (`18.url-credential-judged-trimmed-and-in-any-connector-string.ts`) narrowed to the special schemes; its `reason` names all four spellings, the triple-slash one included. The changeset FROM/TO: FROM spells the triple-slash form (`https:///billing:…@api.billing.example.com/v1`), TO the `scheme://` URL with the secret under `auth: { type, credentialRef }`, and the sentence under it extends the same mapping to the no-slash, one-slash and backslash spellings and to the datasource keys. Both declaration lines are first on the changeset body as the gate reads them.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Scheme-less leading pair mixing `/` and `\` (dev's open question): option A, leave as ruled.** A scheme-less string has no WHATWG reading at all without a base (`new URL()` fails `//u:p@h`, `/\u:p@h` and `\\u:p@h` alike); the `//` reading both doors keep is RFC 3986's network-path reference, in which `\` is not a delimiter, and neither door's consumer resolves a scheme-less value against a special base (`fetch` needs an absolute URL, libsql needs a scheme). The ruling names the special schemes only; reading `/\` as scheme-relative would be a new ruling, not an execution of this one. Nothing slips meanwhile.
- **Residual (2), `packages/cli/src/utils/connection-display.ts` `redactConnectionUrl`:** a print-time label in `os dev` / `os start` / `os serve` that reads the `scheme://` grammar and `new URL()`; it is not one of the two doors the ruling names and is outside this PR's package, so "no other package is touched" is correct scope. It is a follow-up — and because it concerns a credential reaching a log line it is not a public card: it stays with the `security#1` seat under security-findings.md §5/§9 (private field, no-card dispatch). Not a finding on this PR.
- **Verification section written while three readings were pending.** The readings are now in on this head: dogfood battery 417 files / 3462 tests green; `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` exit 0; `check:type-check-debt` exit 0; `--ran` 81/81 accounted for. The check-runs are the gate verdicts and every gate-carrying context is `success` (the ten required contexts included), so landing is not blocked by the body. **Should-fix:** before landing, the seat corrects the body's Verification block to carry those four readings against head `8726545337` (edit the body through the fleet path, read it back, keep the footer as stored), so the PR of record names its readings rather than deferring them to a comment.

### ④ Design judgment

**`authorityStart()` against WHATWG.** The WHATWG special-authority-slashes and special-authority-ignore-slashes states skip every `/` and `\` after `scheme:` for a special scheme, zero included, then enter the authority state; the head's loop is that reading. Probe (55 strings, no suite): mixed-case schemes (`HtTpS:\\`, `WSS:`, `FTP:///`, `HTTP:U:P@H`), four and five slashes, a backslash-only run of four, mixed runs (`https:/\/\`, `http:/\/`), tab inside the scheme, LF after the colon, CR before `//`, surrounding spaces — all read the same userinfo `new URL()` reads. The last-`@` rule matches both WHATWG (`https:u:p@h@i` → `u:p%40h`) and libsql. No string WHATWG reads as credentials is missed (GRAMMAR_LESS 0 of 55). Every divergence is in the refusing direction and was already so on `main` for the `//` spelling: an authority WHATWG ends at `\` (`https://h\path@x`) and an empty userinfo (`https:@h`, which the connector door refuses as it refuses `https://@h`; the datasource door accepts both, no password). A percent-encoded `@` is a delimiter for neither.

**Can a string WHATWG reads as credentials still slip past either door?** None found. The doors judge the cleaned string (`urlAsParsed`), so a tab, LF, CR or surrounding C0/space cannot hide the scheme or the run; the scheme regex is WHATWG's character class; `file` is the one special scheme left out, and WHATWG itself fails a `file://` URL holding a userinfo. The narrowing makes the spec's own refusal real at the exact spellings a URL parser reads credentials from, at the consumer (`fetch`, `new URL()`) that would read them.

**Can a string that is not a URL be falsely refused?** A plain-text `providerConfig` or `auth` string that begins `http:`, `https:`, `ws:`, `wss:` or `ftp:` and holds an `@` before any `/`, `?` or `#` — `http:contact admin@example.com` — is now refused. That is what the ruling orders: WHATWG reads that string as userinfo `contact%20admin` at host `example.com`. The refusal is located at the string, names the parts and never the value, and the author's fix is not to open a note with a scheme. The repo-wide count at `1f13eb3189` is 0; an email with no scheme, a `mailto:` string, a non-special scheme and `file:` are untouched (probe). Accepted consequence of ruling D, not a finding.

Findings: must-fix none; should-fix one (③, the Verification block).

Implemented-by: `claude/sec-hardening-q`
Reviewed-by: `session_01QSeKYn5CmmdShCJifm6WYj`

**VERDICT: PASS**
